standard_prerequisites.name: Inconsistency via closed tableaux
standard_prerequisites.statement: A finite signed assumption set is inconsistent iff it has a closed tableau; inconsistency of a set is witnessed by a finite subset with a closed tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both antecedent inconsistencies are unpacked into closed-tableau witnesses with True A (resp. True not-A) among the assumptions.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Cut rule
standard_prerequisites.statement: A tableau branch may be split on any sentence A into a branch with True A and one with False A.
standard_prerequisites.use: The single Cut application routes each half of the combined tableau to its own closing witness.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 983-986): if Gamma union {A} and Gamma union {not A} are both inconsistent, then Gamma is inconsistent.
Unpacking (proof lines 988-998): finite B_1,...,B_n and C_1,...,C_m in Gamma with {True A, True B_1,...,True B_n} and {True not-A, True C_1,...,True C_m} both closed.

Combined construction (proof lines 998-1015): one combined tableau with assumptions True B_1,...,True B_n, True C_1,...,True C_m, then a single Cut on A; the left branch adds the first tableau below its assumptions (every rule application stays correct since True A is available) and every branch below True A closes; the right branch is completed with the second tableau likewise; hence Gamma is inconsistent.
proof_roadmap: Unpack both inconsistencies into finite closed-tableau witnesses.
Merge the Gamma-side assumptions and apply one Cut on A.
Extend each branch with its witness tableau and conclude closure.
difficulty_reason: Exhaustiveness of tableaux derivability (statement 983-986, proof 988-1031): the complete combined-tableau construction with the Cut routing and both closure arguments carried in span. H2.
